key_insight: The paper shows that quantum circuit expressibility is only meaningful when supported by enough measurement copies, yielding a sample-budget law that links learnable circuit depth to available data.
engineering_relevance: For quantum machine learning systems, it provides a principled way to choose ansatz complexity from data rather than fixed design assumptions, reducing over- or under-parameterized models.
method: Derive a metric-entropy based sample law for states preparable with at most G two-qubit gates.
Define best-G approximation error d_G and approximate circuit complexity C_eta for arbitrary quantum sources.
Prove an agnostic Occam theorem and an adaptive model-selection oracle inequality with matching lower bounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees and lower bounds, showing sample-supported expressibility scales like G_supported ≃ Mε^2 up to logarithmic factors, with saturation near the full tomography limit 2^n.
watch_item: The guarantees are asymptotic and information-theoretic, so practical performance may depend on noise, optimization, and the difficulty of estimating the required approximation error from finite data.
paper_title: Quantum Occam Learning: Sample-Supported Expressibility for Circuit-Based Quantum Learning
